page: Vultr vc2-1c-2gb belongs to the Cloud Compute family and represents an entry-tier virtual server configuration. It provides a single shared x86_64 vCPU from an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 2.0 GB of memory and 55 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU instruction set features AVX, AVX-512F, BMI2, FMA, and AES cryptographic hardware extensions, although hyperthreading is disabled on this single-thread allocation. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes locate the compute and throughput performance in the lower tiers across standardized tests. In stress-ng, single-core and multi-core CPU performance both achieve 1211.89 points, falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories respectively. PassMark tests mirror this profile with an overall CPU score of 1141.0, an encryption score of 437.67, and a database operations score of 285.19. Memory bandwidth evaluates to 85.9 GB/sec for small cached blocks but drops to 7.23 GB/sec read and 5.37 GB/sec write on uncached 256MB blocks.

Application-level measurements indicate 0.67 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 0.78 GB/sec. Data handling throughput reaches 20.76 GB/sec for single-threaded gzip compression and 6.86 GB/sec for bzip3 decompression. When running a small 135M parameter LLM, inference yields 98.76 tokens/sec for prompt ingestion and 24.32 tokens/sec during generation.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the shared-core allocation and modest 2.0 GB RAM footprint trade raw throughput for accessible, low-overhead resource provisioning. The primary limitation stems from the single-threaded CPU configuration and lower memory bandwidth, which restricts high-concurrency tasks. As a result, Vultr vc2-1c-2gb functions effectively for lightweight tasks such as basic web serving, utility cron jobs, small proxy endpoints, testing environments, and low-traffic backends.

The processor incorporates AVX, AVX-512F, and AES extensions, but lacks hyperthreading on its single-core thread allocation, with zero dedicated GPUs. Benchmark scores align the instance with lower performance tiers: stress-ng single-core reaches 1211.89, PassMark CPU yields 1141.0, and large-block memory read bandwidth measures 7.23 GB/sec.
